facts.text: Amherst operates an open curriculum with no core curriculum and no general distribution requirements, allowing students to choose classes freely with faculty guidance.

sources.title: Our Open Curriculum | Amherst College
sources.quote: Amherst has no distribution requirements and no core curriculum. Instead, students choose the courses that matter most to them.

facts.text: Amherst has an open curriculum with no general distribution requirements or core courses outside of an initial first-year seminar and major coursework.

sources.title: Academics | Amherst College
sources.quote: To graduate, students must complete four years of coursework, but apart from one first-year seminar and the required courses for their major, they are free to choose their classes.

facts.text: Through the Five College Consortium, Amherst students have cross-registration access to more than 6,000 courses across Smith, Mount Holyoke, Hampshire, and UMass Amherst.

sources.title: Academics | Amherst College
sources.quote: Amherst students can choose among more than 6,000 courses for credit at four nearby schools: Smith, Mount Holyoke, and Hampshire Colleges, and the University of Massachusetts Amherst.
